questions.questionText:
A government uses different supply-side policy measures to improve economic performance.
Which policy measure would not satisfy one of the government’s macroeconomic aims?

options.text: changing the tax system which leads to more tax evasion
encouraging foreign investment which improves the balance of payments
privatising state industries which increases economic growth
retraining redundant workers which lowers unemployment

questions.questionText: What could cause an increase in demand for a factor of production?

options.text: decrease in the efficiency of the factor of production
decrease in the price of an alternative factor of production
increase in the demand for the good or service produced
increase in the price of the factor of production

questions.questionText:
Which components, in addition to Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per head, are included in the
Human Development Index (HDI)?

options.text: average earnings and inequalities of incomes
balance of trade and balance of payments
life expectancy at birth and expected years of schooling
size of population and age structure of population

questions.questionText:
The US government introduces tariffs on steel imported from China. This increases the price of
imported Chinese steel.
Whose income would be likely to increase as a direct result?
Chinese steel
US government
producers

options.text: yes yes
yes no
no yes
no no

questions.questionText:
A government retrains unemployed industrial workers to increase employment opportunities. The
policy may have adverse effects on other government macroeconomic aims.
What illustrates this situation?

options.text: Better skilled workers may increase productivity and improve economic growth.
Increased wage-earning capacity may lead to demand-pull inflation.
More employed workers may reduce government expenditure on benefit payments.
Near full employment may result in a more stable balance of payments.

questions.questionText:
The table shows the world output of iron ore and the average yearly price for four years.
world output of iron ore average yearly price
year
(billion tonnes) ($ per tonne)
year 1 2.86 128
year 2 2.98 135
year 3 2.22 97
year 4 2.28 95
What can be concluded about the relationship between world output of iron ore and the average
yearly price over the four years?
average
world output
yearly price

options.text: highest highest
highest lowest
lowest highest
lowest lowest

questions.questionText:
A firm has a high price elasticity of supply for its product.
What does this indicate?

options.text: It can increase revenue by reducing the price.
It can quickly respond to changes in price.
It keeps very low volumes of product in stock.
It produces a good that has close substitutes.

questions.questionText:
A manufacturer of medical supplies benefits from improved road links to its main markets.
What benefit definitely occurs as a result?

options.text: increased average revenue
increased external economies of scale
increased internal economies of scale
increased market share

questions.questionText:
Which row shows an essential characteristic of competitive markets and monopoly markets?
competitive markets monopoly markets

options.text: many buyers single seller
many sellers single buyer
single buyer many buyers
single seller many sellers

questions.questionText:
A student has nothing to do on a Friday evening. She withdraws $5 from the $100 she has in a
savings account and buys a present to take to a party, to which admission is free.
What does this involve?

options.text: an opportunity cost equal to $95
an opportunity cost equal to other goods she could have bought for $5
no opportunity cost, as entrance to the party is free
no opportunity cost, as she had no better way of using the time

questions.questionText:
The development of artificial intelligence in machines raises the productivity of capital.
What will be the effect of this?

options.text: The costs of production will increase.
The demand for capital will increase.
The price of capital will fall.
The supply of capital will decrease.

questions.questionText:
Which combination is necessary for the construction of a consumer prices index?
a base year price stability weights

options.text: yes yes yes
yes no yes
yes no no
no yes yes

questions.questionText:
A government removed the quota on goods imported into the country.
What is the most likely result of this?

options.text: a decrease in demand for domestic production
a decrease in domestic unemployment
a decrease in exports
a decrease in the balance of trade deficit

questions.questionText: What is an advantage of a country having a market economic system with a large private sector?

options.text: Firms can become unprofitable if they do not produce what consumers want.
Market forces often fail to ensure maximum benefits for society.
Some goods may not be provided at all or not in sufficient quantity.
There is an unequal distribution of income which can increase over time.

questions.questionText: What is an example of a fiscal policy measure?

options.text: increasing the exchange rate
reducing the power of trade unions
reducing the rate of corporation tax
setting a lower interest rate

questions.questionText: Why would an increase in the interest rate potentially lead to lower inflation?

options.text: Consumers will be more willing to save when interest rates are high.
Consumers will be more willing to spend when interest rates are high.
Producers will be more willing to borrow from banks when interest rates are high.
Producers will be more willing to invest when interest rates are high.

questions.questionText: Which government action will not add directly to the quantity or quality of human resources?

options.text: improvement in health facilities
investment in education and training
provision of better food and nutrition
reclamation of land from the sea

questions.questionText: What is a likely cause of economic growth?

options.text: decreased employment
decreased investment
decreased productivity
decreased taxation

questions.questionText:
The table shows how three people, X, Y and Z, spend their income.
person X person Y person Z
food, clothing and housing 30% 25% 50%
entertainment and leisure 35% 35% 25%
luxury goods 35% 40% 25%
What is the likely order of income, from lowest income to highest income, for these three people?

options.text: Y  X  Z
Y  Z  X
Z  X  Y
Z  Y  X

questions.questionText: Why would standards of living fall when there is a recession?

options.text: The government would increase taxes to combat the recession.
The purchasing power of households would fall.
The value of the domestic currency would increase.
There would be a rise in the level of immigration.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of an economy’s production possibility curve (PPC)?

options.text: It answers the question of what to produce in an economy.
It enables microeconomic decisions to be taken by firms.
It measures the supply of goods and services available in an economy.
It shows the productive capacity in an economy at a point in time.

questions.questionText:
The governments of low-income countries often allow foreign multinational companies (MNCs) to
mine minerals in their country.
Which conflict between benefit and cost might this cause the low-income countries?
benefit cost

options.text: improved balance of trade training by the MNCs
higher employment loss of a finite resource
increased profits for the MNCs efficient production
more sustainable development economic growth

questions.questionText:
The table shows some economic indicators.
Which increase in the first indicator is most likely to lead to an increase in the second indicator?
first indicator second indicator

options.text: budget surplus consumer saving
consumer spending unemployment
inflation trade surplus
productivity living standards

questions.questionText: What is the definition of foreign exchange rate?

options.text: the difference between emigration and immigration
the difference between the values of imports and exports
the price of one currency in terms of another
the price of one good in terms of another

questions.questionText:
Which activity is correctly linked to the organisation that provides it?
organisation activity

options.text: central bank regulate the rate of inflation
central bank set direct tax rates
commercial bank manage the government’s financial accounts
commercial bank safeguard the country’s foreign reserves

questions.questionText: Which topic is not included in microeconomics?

options.text: consumer demand
economies of scale
forms of competition
inflation

questions.questionText: What is likely to cause an immediate decrease in the size of the labour force?

options.text: a fall in the average size of families
a fall in the birth rate
a reduction in the age of retirement
